sentences.text:
Erick Joyel William vs State Of Haryana on 12 December, 2024
 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166240
Crm-M-49846-2024 1
 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana

At Chandigarh
102 Crm-M-49846-2024
 Date of Decision : December 12, 2024
Erick Joyel William -Petitioner
 V/S
State Of Haryana -Respondent
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Tiwari
Present: Mr. Shinoj K Narayanan, Advocate (Through V.C.)
 for the petitioner.
 Mr. Rajesh Gaur, Addl. A.G., Haryana.
 ***
Kuldeep Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1.

On 07.11.2024, this Court had passed the hereinafter extracted order, upon the instant petition:-
"1.

Through the instant petition, as instituted under Section 482 of the B.N.S.S.,
2023, the petitioner seeks the concession of anticipatory bail, in case FIR No.31 dated 19.03.2024, under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Cyber Crime Ballabgarh, District Faridabad.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner inter alia submits that, a perusal of the FIR makes it abundantly clear that, no money of the complainant has been embezzled,
rather the allegation is that, the profit of  5,62,500/-, as earned by the complainant by carrying out the activities directed by the petitioner, has not been deposited in his bank account.
Therefore, the above allegation do not constitute any offence of cyber crime.
Mr. Rajesh Gaur, Addl. A.G., Haryana, accepts notice on behalf of respondent-State of Haryana.

sentences.text: In the meantime, the petitioner is directed to join the investigation and to appear before the investigating agency, as and when called upon to do so.
In the event of his arrest, he shall be admitted to interim bail on his furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166240 Arresting/Investigating Officer.
The petitioner shall abide by the terms and conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of the B.N.S.S., 2023."

2. Thereafter, the learned State counsel filed the status report dated 29.11.2024, wherein became voiced that, although the petitioner joined the investigation, however, he did not cooperate with the investigating officer inasmuch as he remained evasive to most of the questions put to him.
3. Perusal of the status report (supra) reveals that, the questions put to the petitioner were self inculpatory, which cannot be expected from the petitioner to be answered.
It will not be read granting petitioner indefinite protection from arrest.
It shall be confined to the FIR mentioned ibid and will not operate in respect of any other incident that involves commission of an offence.
5. Needless to say that anything observed hereinabove shall not be construed to be an opinion on the merits of the case.

(KULDEEP TIWARI)
